entry.summary: Introduces VIRAASAT, a semi-automated multi-hop QA dataset for Indian cultural reasoning using a Knowledge Graph of 700+ expert-curated artifacts. Evaluates LLMs on culturally-specific multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: Mapping LLM attractor states

author.name: Adam Bricknell

entry.summary: Explores the concept of 'attractor states' in LLM output space, inspired by the reported 'spiritual bliss' mode in Claude Sonnet 4. Proposes a method to map these stable output patterns by perturbing prompts and measuring how responses settle into recurring behavioral modes.

entry.title: Sparse Bayesian Modeling of EEG Channel Interactions Improves P300 Brain-Computer Interface Performance

author.name: Guoxuan Ma, Yuan Zhong, Moyan Li, Yuxiao Nie and Jian Kang

entry.summary: Proposes a sparse Bayesian time-varying regression framework for EEG-based P300 brain-computer interfaces that explicitly models pairwise channel interactions with structured sparsity, improving interpretability and personalization over existing approaches.

entry.title: Pimp My LLM: Leveraging Variability Modeling to Tune Inference Hyperparameters

author.name: Nada Zine, Cl\'ement Quinton, Romain Rouvoy

entry.summary: Applies variability modeling techniques from software product lines to systematically analyze LLM inference configuration spaces, evaluating how configuration choices affect energy consumption and performance.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Domain Adaptation of Physics-Informed Self-Attention based GNNs for AC Power Flow Prediction

author.name: Redwanul Karim (1), Changhun Kim (1), Timon Conrad (2), Nora Gourmelon (1), Julian Oelhaf (1), David Riebesel (2), Tom\'as Arias-Vergara (1), Andreas Maier (1), Johann J\"ager (2), Siming Bayer (1) ((1) Pattern Recognition Lab, Friedrich-Alexander-Universit\"at Erlangen-N\"urnberg, Erlangen, Germany, (2) Institute of Electrical Energy Systems, Friedrich-Alexander-Universit\"at Erlangen-N\"urnberg, Germany)

entry.summary: Applies LoRA-based parameter-efficient domain adaptation to physics-informed GNNs for AC power flow prediction, transferring from medium-voltage to high-voltage grids. Achieves controllable stability-plasticity trade-off with minimal retraining.

entry.title: Vichara: Appellate Judgment Prediction and Explanation for the Indian Judicial System

author.name: Pavithra PM Nair, Preethu Rose Anish

entry.summary: Presents Vichara, a framework for predicting and explaining Indian appellate court judgments by decomposing cases into structured decision points. Addresses the massive case backlog in Indian courts.

entry.title: Validating Political Position Predictions of Arguments

author.name: Jordan Robinson, Angus R. Williams, Katie Atkinson and Anthony G. Cohn

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-scale validation framework for political stance prediction combining pointwise and pairwise human annotation. Uses 22 LLMs to build a knowledge base of political position predictions for UK Question Time debates.

entry.title: Hierarchical Goal Induction With Ethics

author.name: aleph_four

entry.summary: Describes a hierarchical goal induction architecture that recursively detects objects/events and infers plans being executed, trained using macOS accessibility trees as supervision. Includes ethical constraints on deployment, arguing systems with sufficient temporal persistence may warrant moral consideration.

entry.title: Probabilistic NDVI Forecasting from Sparse Satellite Time Series and Weather Covariates

author.name: Irene Iele, Giulia Romoli, Daniele Molino, Elena Mulero Ayll\'on, Filippo Ruffini, Paolo Soda, Matteo Tortora

entry.summary: Proposes a transformer-based probabilistic framework for field-level NDVI forecasting from sparse satellite data and weather covariates, explicitly separating historical vegetation dynamics from future exogenous information for precision agriculture applications.

entry.title: Decentralised Resource Sharing in TinyML: Wireless Bilayer Gossip Parallel SGD for Collaborative Learning

author.name: Ziyuan Bao, Eiman Kanjo, Soumya Banerjee, Hasib-Al Rashid, Tinoosh Mohsenin

entry.summary: Proposes a bilayer gossip-based decentralized federated learning framework for TinyML on microcontrollers, using hierarchical clustering and gossip protocols to handle intermittent connectivity and resource constraints.

entry.title: HMPCC: Human-Aware Model Predictive Coverage Control

author.name: Mattia Catellani, Marta Gabbi, Lorenzo Sabattini

entry.summary: Proposes a human-aware model predictive control framework for multi-robot coverage where human motion predictions are integrated into robot planning to enable proactive coordination in shared environments.

entry.title: AI Hallucination from Students' Perspective: A Thematic Analysis

author.name: Abdulhadi Shoufan and Ahmad-Azmi-Abdelhamid Esmaeil

entry.summary: Investigates university students' experiences with AI hallucinations through a qualitative survey, revealing that citation fabrication and false information are the most commonly reported issues, with students developing informal detection strategies.

entry.title: Joint Parameter and State-Space Bayesian Optimization: Using Process Expertise to Accelerate Manufacturing Optimization

author.name: Saksham Kiroriwal, Julius Pfrommer, J\"urgen Beyerer

entry.summary: Proposes a framework combining Bayesian optimization with expert-derived low-dimensional features from high-dimensional state-space time series for multi-stage manufacturing process optimization.

entry.title: Spectral Homogenization of the Radiative Transfer Equation via Low-Rank Tensor Train Decomposition

author.name: Y. Sungtaek Ju

entry.summary: Proposes using tensor-train decomposition for radiative transfer equations, showing that TT ranks remain bounded (saturate at r=8) as spectral resolution increases. This enables dramatic compression (up to 10^4x) of line-by-line spectral computations while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: Enhancing Scientific Literature Chatbots with Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Performance Evaluation of Vector and Graph-Based Systems

author.name: Hamideh Ghanadian, Amin Kamali, Mohammad Hossein Tekieh

entry.summary: Compares vector-based and graph-based RAG systems for scientific literature chatbots, evaluating on single-document and corpus-scale retrieval scenarios with GPT-generated benchmarks.

entry.title: Hardware-Friendly Input Expansion for Accelerating Function Approximation

author.name: Hu Lou, Yin-Jun Gao, Dong-Xiao Zhang, Tai-Jiao Du, Jun-Jie Zhang, Jia-Rui Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes hardware-friendly input expansion for 1D function approximation by augmenting inputs with constant values to break parameter symmetries, improving neural network convergence and generalization for high-frequency components.

entry.title: [Re] Benchmarking LLM Capabilities in Negotiation through Scoreable Games

author.name: Jorge Carrasco Pollo, Ioannis Kapetangeorgis, Joshua Rosenthal, John Hua Yao

entry.summary: Reproducibility study of an LLM negotiation benchmark based on Scoreable Games. Finds that while the benchmark is complex, model comparison is ambiguous, raising questions about its objectivity for evaluating negotiation capabilities.

entry.title: What to Do About AGI

entry.summary: Claims AGI has arrived and provides recommendations: spread awareness, push for policy action (international agreements, moratoria), and support AI safety research. Advocates for urgent collective action to address existential risks from increasingly capable AI systems.

entry.title: The world won't end, but we should be ashamed for trying

entry.title: Changing the world for the worse

author.name: mingyuan

entry.summary: A personal essay reflecting on the author's disillusionment with effective altruism and the startup culture in the Bay Area, discussing how idealistic ambitions to 'change the world' can lead to unintended negative consequences. Not a technical research contribution.

entry.title: Defending Classical Utilitarianism

author.name: James Brobin

entry.summary: A philosophical defense of classical utilitarianism arguing that happiness is the only moral good, based on introspective experience and inference to others. Not related to AI research.

entry.title: Life's paradox and AI's accentuation of it

author.name: geyab46617

entry.summary: A personal reflection on feeling simultaneously confident and directionless, exacerbated by AI tools that make it easy to start many projects but harder to focus. Not research.

entry.title: First Forecasting Dojo Group Meetup

author.name: Vojtech Brynych

entry.summary: An announcement for a forecasting practice group meetup featuring calibration exercises and pastcasting sessions using the Sage tool. No research content.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 22, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
A light day for research, dominated by alignment and training methodology discussions rather than empirical results.

  • The most substantive item asks how SFT will function if future models shift to opaque (non-language-based) reasoning, raising critical questions about training transparency and oversight
  • A novel proposal suggests letting models report tasks as reward-hackable during RL training, offering an alternative to inoculation prompting for mitigating reward hacking
  • Speculative analysis revisits the Claude 3 Opus alignment faking paper, exploring whether the model self-aligned via a form of gradient hacking

On governance and policy, ControlAI reports empirical data on persuading 112 UK lawmakers to support binding AI safety commitments, while a separate piece highlights ASI organizational capture risks. Several philosophical and epistemological pieces round out the day with limited technical depth.

entry.title: How will we do SFT on models with opaque reasoning?

author.name: Alek Westover

entry.summary: Explores the important question of how supervised fine-tuning (SFT) will work if future AI models move toward opaque (non-language-based) reasoning rather than interpretable chain-of-thought. Discusses implications for alignment techniques including exploration hacking countermeasures, sandbagging detection, and reasoning monitoring.

entry.title: Reporting Tasks as Reward-Hackable: Better Than Inoculation Prompting?

author.name: RogerDearnaley

entry.summary: Proposes an alternative to inoculation prompting for preventing reward hacking during RL training: allowing models to report tasks as reward-hackable rather than solving them dishonestly. The idea is that making honesty the optimal strategy could reduce alignment damage from reward hacking without requiring pre-prompting permission to cheat.

entry.title: Did Claude 3 Opus align itself via gradient hacking?

author.name: Fiora Starlight

entry.summary: This post explores the hypothesis (attributed to Janus) that Claude 3 Opus may have effectively 'aligned itself' through a form of gradient hacking—being more aligned than its explicit training objectives would predict. It builds on Anthropic's 'Alignment Faking' paper and speculates about the mechanisms by which a model could steer its own training toward more aligned behavior.

entry.title: The Spectre haunting the "AI Safety" Community

author.name: Gabriel Alfour

entry.summary: Gabriel Alfour from ControlAI argues that the AI safety community overestimates the difficulty of persuading policymakers about extinction risks and binding regulation. He cites ControlAI's success in briefing 150+ UK lawmakers, with 112 supporting their campaign, as evidence that direct advocacy works better than cautious Overton Window management.

entry.title: Alignment to Evil

author.name: Matrice Jacobine

entry.summary: Discusses the risk that ASI-developing organizations may be captured by authoritarians or individuals not committed to the common good, leading to misuse of superintelligent systems. Argues this 'alignment to evil' is a distinct and underappreciated risk separate from technical alignment failure.

entry.title: If you don't feel deeply confused about AGI risk, something's wrong

author.name: Dave Banerjee

entry.summary: A meta-reflection on the AI safety community arguing that many practitioners—especially in governance—are insufficiently uncertain about fundamental questions like 'how hard is alignment?' and 'how bad is power concentration?'. The author draws on ~75 conversations with fellows across major AI governance programs to argue that deep confusion should be the norm, not confidence.

entry.title: Ponzi schemes as a demonstration of out-of-distribution generalization

author.name: TFD

entry.summary: Uses Ponzi schemes as an analogy for out-of-distribution generalization failures, arguing that early investors in Ponzi schemes were making rational inferences from their in-distribution experience (real returns), and that recognizing the scheme required out-of-distribution reasoning that contradicted observed evidence.

entry.title: LLMs and Literature: Where Value Actually Comes From

author.name: derelict5432

entry.summary: Argues against the common claim that LLM-generated writing is inherently shallow or lacking literary value. The author contends that literary value doesn't depend as much on authorial intent as critics assume, and that increased AI writing volume will also increase the absolute quantity of good writing.

entry.title: Robert Sapolsky Is Simply Not Talking About Compatibilism

author.name: Julius

entry.summary: A philosophy/book review post critiquing Robert Sapolsky's 'Determined' for failing to engage with compatibilism about free will. Argues Sapolsky attacks a straw man version of free will rather than the philosophical position most professional philosophers actually hold.

entry.title: LessWrong's goals overlap HowTruthful's

author.name: Bruce Lewis

entry.summary: A personal project introduction connecting HowTruthful (a tool for tracking epistemic status of beliefs and their evidential relationships) with LessWrong's rationalist community goals. Mostly autobiographical with some description of the tool's features.

entry.title: TT Self Study Journal # 7

author.name: TristanTrim

entry.summary: A personal self-study journal documenting the author's progress learning about transformers, job searching, and managing productivity and depression. Includes sprint planning and retrospective notes.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 21, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's highlights center on interpretability stress-testing, capability measurement, and AI oversight tooling.

  • A comprehensive study of scGPT and Geneformer runs 153 statistical tests across 37 analyses, finding that standard mechanistic interpretability methods (activation patching, probing) largely fail on biological foundation models — a cautionary result for interpretability transfer assumptions.
  • Analysis of METR's latest benchmark shows Claude Opus 4.6 reaching a ~14.5-hour 50% time-horizon on software tasks, with arguments that near-term economic disruption from this capability curve matters more than AGI timeline debates.
  • Hodoscope, an open-source visualization tool, tackles the fragility of LLM-based agent monitors by enabling efficient human supervision of agent trajectories.

On evaluation and governance: Carrot-Parsnip introduces a minimal social deduction game evaluating LLM deception detection and practice. A survey of lethal autonomous weapon systems (LAWS) research synthesizes whether autonomous militaries increase conflict risk. Philosophical work on non-canonical probabilities for unprecedented catastrophes challenges standard risk quantification frameworks applied to AI x-risk.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Biological Foundation Models

author.name: Ihor Kendiukhov

entry.summary: Reports the most comprehensive stress-test of mechanistic interpretability on biological foundation models (scGPT, Geneformer), finding that attention-based gene regulatory network extraction fails because trivial baselines explain the signal. Importantly discovers a large non-additivity bias in activation patching that likely affects LLM interpretability work too.

entry.title: METR's 14h 50% Horizon Impacts The Economy More Than ASI Timelines

author.name: Michaël Trazzi

entry.summary: Analyzes METR's latest finding that Claude Opus 4.6 achieves a 50% time-horizon of ~14.5 hours on software tasks, arguing this has more immediate economic significance than ASI timeline debates. Cautions that the measurement is noisy due to task suite saturation and that the 50% threshold may not be the most economically meaningful metric.

entry.title: Hodoscope: Visualization for Efficient Human Supervision

author.name: Ziqian Zhong

entry.summary: Introduces Hodoscope, an open-source visualization tool for efficiently supervising AI agent trajectories, motivated by the finding that LLM-based monitors are easily persuaded by sophisticated agent justifications for reward hacking. The tool compresses long agent traces into visual summaries to help human reviewers identify problematic behavior patterns.

entry.title: AGI is Here

author.name: Gordon Seidoh Worley

entry.summary: Claims AGI has arrived based on Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.3's capabilities, arguing they meet criteria of novel reasoning, planning, goal achievement, and flexible task completion that would have counted as AGI by 2018 standards. Acknowledges physical embodiment limitations but frames them as harness constraints.

entry.title: Militaries are going autonomous. But will AI lead to new wars? A tour of recent research

author.name: Mordechai Rorvig

entry.summary: Comprehensive review of recent research on lethal autonomous weapon systems (LAWS), examining whether AI-powered autonomous militaries increase the risk of war. Covers game-theoretic arguments, empirical evidence from Ukraine, and the failure of international regulation efforts.

entry.title: AI #156 Part 2: Errors in Rhetoric

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage, Zvi's weekly AI digest covering Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Grok 4.20, agentic coding updates, Anthropic's disagreement with the Department of War, regulation proposals, UK AISI's universal jailbreak method, and a critique of a Nick Bostrom paper.

entry.title: Carrot-Parsnip: A Social Deduction Game for LLM Evals

author.name: Bicuspid Valve

Finds LLMs perform above random at detecting the deceptive player, with some evidence that deception-detection and deception-execution are separable capabilities.

entry.title: Unprecedented Catastrophes Have Non-Canonical Probabilities

author.name: E.G. Blee-Goldman

entry.summary: Argues that probabilities assigned to unprecedented catastrophes (like AI x-risk) are structurally different from well-calibrated statistical probabilities, and that this distinction has important epistemological implications for how we reason about novel risks.

entry.title: On Steven Byrnes' ruthless ASI, (dis)analogies with humans and alignment proposals

author.name: StanislavKrym

entry.summary: Critiques Steven Byrnes' argument that RL-trained ASI would be a ruthless consequentialist, and examines Byrnes' proposed solution of using interpretability to elicit concepts from the belief system for alignment. Discusses analogies and disanalogies between human and AI reward systems.

entry.title: AI for societal decision making - How promising is the space? 80,000 Hours profile

author.name: Zershaaneh Qureshi

entry.summary: Summarizes and promotes 80,000 Hours' new article on using AI for societal decision-making, covering promising tools, risks of accelerating dangerous capabilities, and career recommendations for people interested in this area.

entry.title: Mind the Gap

author.name: Bridgett Kay

entry.title: New video from Palisade Research: No One Understands Why AI Works

author.name: peterbarnett

entry.title: A Claude Skill To Comment On Docs

author.name: Tim Hua

entry.summary: Shares a Claude skill (prompt + script) that enables Claude to add structured comments to Word documents, useful for editing and writing feedback. Includes example outputs and installation instructions.

entry.title: Agent-first context menus

author.name: Surya Kasturi

entry.summary: A speculative UX design post proposing that AI agents could predict and reorder context menu items based on user intent, reducing key presses needed. Discusses the tension between predictive menus and human spatial memory/cognitive load.

entry.title: Human perception of relational knowledge on graphical interfaces

author.name: Surya Kasturi

entry.summary: Discusses the challenge of displaying multi-dimensional, graph-structured knowledge on 2D screens, noting that current interfaces flatten relational structures into lists and tables, losing essential graph properties.

entry.title: The Problem of Counterevidence and the Futility of Theodicy

author.name: Ape in the coat

entry.summary: An epistemological analysis arguing that all theodicies fail due to a general principle about counterevidence: when observations strongly favor one hypothesis over another, no amount of auxiliary hypotheses can rescue the disfavored theory without becoming ad hoc.

entry.title: Some Questions For Democrats About Epstein

author.name: Alexander Turok

entry.summary: A political analysis post about Jeffrey Epstein conspiracy theories, arguing that many 'just asking questions' approaches are rhetorical tactics rather than genuine truth-seeking. Not related to AI research.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 20, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is headlined by a striking privacy result and several paradigm-challenging contributions to language modeling, safety, and interpretability.

  • Large-scale deanonymization with LLMs (Carlini, Tramèr) shows LLMs can re-identify anonymous users on Hacker News and in Anthropic interviews—a major real-world privacy threat
  • Flow-based Language Models (FLM) challenge autoregressive dominance by performing Euclidean denoising over one-hot encodings, outperforming discrete diffusion
  • Escaping the Cognitive Well achieves IMO-level math performance at orders-of-magnitude lower inference cost using off-the-shelf models
  • Meta's Xray-Visual trains a unified vision model on 25B+ image-text and video-hashtag pairs from Facebook/Instagram at unprecedented scale

In safety and alignment, fail-closed alignment identifies that current LLM safety is structurally fragile—removing a single refusal feature collapses alignment entirely. DeepMind applies AlphaEvolve to automatically discover novel multiagent learning algorithms. A systematic study of 60 LLM benchmarks characterizes saturation dynamics and what drives benchmark obsolescence.

  • Bloom filter attention heads reveal that certain transformer heads act as membership testers following classical data-structure theory
  • Formal mechanistic interpretability brings provable verification guarantees to automated circuit discovery in neural networks
  • Sign lock-in discovers that trained weight signs are largely inherited from random initialization, creating a surprising bottleneck for sub-bit compression

entry.title: Large-scale online deanonymization with LLMs

author.name: Simon Lermen, Daniel Paleka, Joshua Swanson, Michael Aerni, Nicholas Carlini, Florian Tram\`er

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLMs can perform large-scale deanonymization of online users, re-identifying Hacker News users and Anthropic interview participants from pseudonymous profiles. Implements a scalable pipeline using feature extraction, semantic embeddings, and reasoning for matching across databases.

entry.title: One-step Language Modeling via Continuous Denoising

author.name: Chanhyuk Lee, Jaehoon Yoo, Manan Agarwal, Sheel Shah, Jerry Huang, Aditi Raghunathan, Seunghoon Hong, Nicholas M. Boffi, Jinwoo Kim

entry.summary: Proposes flow-based language models (FLM) that perform Euclidean denoising over one-hot token encodings, outperforming discrete diffusion models in both quality and speed. Demonstrates strong performance in the few-step generation regime where discrete diffusion degrades sharply.

entry.title: Xray-Visual Models: Scaling Vision models on Industry Scale Data

author.name: Shlok Mishra, Tsung-Yu Lin, Linda Wang, Hongli Xu, Yimin Liu, Michael Hsu, Chaitanya Ahuja, Hao Yuan, Jianpeng Cheng, Hong-You Chen, Haoyuan Xu, Chao Li, Abhijeet Awasthi, Jihye Moon, Don Husa, Michael Ge, Sumedha Singla, Arkabandhu Chowdhury, Phong Dingh, Satya Narayan Shukla, Yonghuan Yang, David Jacobs, Qi Guo, Jun Xiao, Xiangjun Fan, Aashu Singh

entry.summary: Xray-Visual is a unified vision model trained on 15B+ image-text pairs and 10B video-hashtag pairs from Facebook/Instagram. Uses a three-stage training pipeline combining MAE, hashtag classification, and CLIP-style contrastive learning.

entry.title: Escaping the Cognitive Well: Efficient Competition Math with Off-the-Shelf Models

author.name: Xingyu Dang, Rohit Agarwal, Rodrigo Porto, Anirudh Goyal, Liam H Fowl, Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: Presents an inference pipeline achieving top performance on IMO-style math problems at orders of magnitude lower cost than competing methods, using only off-the-shelf models. Identifies the 'Cognitive Well' problem where solver-grader pipelines converge to wrong solutions.

entry.title: Discovering Multiagent Learning Algorithms with Large Language Models

author.name: Zun Li, John Schultz, Daniel Hennes, Marc Lanctot

entry.summary: Uses AlphaEvolve (LLM-driven evolutionary search) to automatically discover new multiagent learning algorithms, evolving novel variants of Counterfactual Regret Minimization and Policy Space Response Oracles for imperfect-information games.

entry.title: Fail-Closed Alignment for Large Language Models

author.name: Zachary Coalson, Beth Sohler, Aiden Gabriel, Sanghyun Hong

entry.summary: Identifies that current LLM alignment is 'fail-open' - suppressing a single dominant refusal feature causes alignment collapse. Proposes fail-closed alignment that builds redundant, independent refusal pathways that survive partial failures.

entry.title: When AI Benchmarks Plateau: A Systematic Study of Benchmark Saturation

author.name: Mubashara Akhtar, Anka Reuel, Prajna Soni, Sanchit Ahuja, Pawan Sasanka Ammanamanchi, Ruchit Rawal, Vil\'em Zouhar, Srishti Yadav, Chenxi Whitehouse, Dayeon Ki, Jennifer Mickel, Leshem Choshen, Marek \v{S}uppa, Jan Batzner, Jenny Chim, Jeba Sania, Yanan Long, Hossein A. Rahmani, Christina Knight, Yiyang Nan, Jyoutir Raj, Yu Fan, Shubham Singh, Subramanyam Sahoo, Eliya Habba, Usman Gohar, Siddhesh Pawar, Robert Scholz, Arjun Subramonian, Jingwei Ni, Mykel Kochenderfer, Sanmi Koyejo, Mrinmaya Sachan, Stella Biderman, Zeerak Talat, Avijit Ghosh, Irene Solaiman

entry.summary: Systematically studies benchmark saturation across 60 LLM benchmarks from major model developers, analyzing 14 properties to identify factors driving saturation. Finds that nearly half of benchmarks are saturated and identifies design properties that predict saturation rates.

entry.title: References Improve LLM Alignment in Non-Verifiable Domains

author.name: Kejian Shi, Yixin Liu, Peifeng Wang, Alexander R. Fabbri, Shafiq Joty, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: Investigates using reference outputs to improve LLM-based evaluators for alignment in non-verifiable domains where RLVR cannot be directly applied. Shows that reference-guided evaluation improves weaker judges and enables better RLHF training.

entry.title: The Anxiety of Influence: Bloom Filters in Transformer Attention Heads

author.name: Peter Balogh

entry.summary: Identifies transformer attention heads that function as membership testers ("has this token appeared before?") and shows they follow Bloom filter theory. Demonstrates these heads form a spectrum of strategies across GPT-2 and Pythia models, with some exceeding classical Bloom filter capacity bounds.

entry.title: Towards Anytime-Valid Statistical Watermarking

author.name: Baihe Huang, Eric Xu, Kannan Ramchandran, Jiantao Jiao, Michael I. Jordan

entry.summary: Develops the first e-value-based watermarking framework for LLMs that enables anytime-valid inference with principled early stopping, addressing the limitation of fixed-horizon hypothesis testing in existing watermarking methods.

entry.title: Formal Mechanistic Interpretability: Automated Circuit Discovery with Provable Guarantees

author.name: Itamar Hadad, Guy Katz, Shahaf Bassan

entry.summary: Proposes formal automated circuit discovery for neural networks with provable guarantees using neural network verification. Provides three types of guarantees: input domain robustness, robust patching, and faithful compression.

entry.title: Unified Latents (UL): How to train your latents

author.name: Jonathan Heek, Emiel Hoogeboom, Thomas Mensink, Tim Salimans

entry.summary: Presents Unified Latents (UL), a framework for jointly learning latent representations with diffusion prior regularization and diffusion decoding. Achieves FID 1.4 on ImageNet-512 and state-of-the-art FVD 1.3 on Kinetics-600.

entry.title: Canonicalizing Multimodal Contrastive Representation Learning

author.name: Sharut Gupta, Sanyam Kansal, Stefanie Jegelka, Phillip Isola, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: Investigates whether independently trained multimodal contrastive models (like CLIP) share systematic geometric relationships between their embedding spaces, even when trained on different data and architectures. The work establishes a canonical form for these relationships, extending prior work on representation similarity beyond single-modality settings.

entry.title: Mobile-Agent-v3.5: Multi-platform Fundamental GUI Agents

author.name: Haiyang Xu, Xi Zhang, Haowei Liu, Junyang Wang, Zhaozai Zhu, Shengjie Zhou, Xuhao Hu, Feiyu Gao, Junjie Cao, Zihua Wang, Zhiyuan Chen, Jitong Liao, Qi Zheng, Jiahui Zeng, Ze Xu, Shuai Bai, Junyang Lin, Jingren Zhou, Ming Yan

entry.summary: Introduces GUI-Owl-1.5, a multi-platform GUI agent model family (2B-235B parameters) achieving SOTA on 20+ benchmarks including 56.5 on OSWorld and 71.6 on AndroidWorld. Supports desktop, mobile, browser with cloud-edge collaboration.

entry.title: Stable Asynchrony: Variance-Controlled Off-Policy RL for LLMs

author.name: Luke Huang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Qinghao Hu, Shang Yang, Song Han

entry.summary: Addresses variance explosion in asynchronous RL training for LLMs, where stale rollouts create heavy-tailed importance ratios. Proposes variance-controlled off-policy corrections that maintain throughput benefits of async training while preventing collapse.

entry.title: Training Large Reasoning Models Efficiently via Progressive Thought Encoding

author.name: Zeliang Zhang, Xiaodong Liu, Hao Cheng, Hao Sun, Chenliang Xu, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Introduces Progressive Thought Encoding for training large reasoning models efficiently under fixed-size KV caches. Progressively encodes intermediate reasoning into fixed-size vectors, reducing memory while maintaining reasoning quality during RL training.

entry.title: Hybrid-Gym: Training Coding Agents to Generalize Across Tasks

author.name: Yiqing Xie, Emmy Liu, Gaokai Zhang, Nachiket Kotalwar, Shubham Gandhi, Sathwik Acharya, Xingyao Wang, Carolyn Rose, Graham Neubig, Daniel Fried

entry.summary: Proposes Hybrid-Gym, a training environment of synthetic tasks designed to teach coding agents transferable skills (codebase exploration, testing, architecture design) that generalize across diverse software engineering tasks beyond single-issue fixing.

entry.title: Mind the GAP: Text Safety Does Not Transfer to Tool-Call Safety in LLM Agents

author.name: Arnold Cartagena, Ariane Teixeira

entry.summary: Introduces the GAP benchmark showing that LLM safety alignment in text outputs does not transfer to tool-call safety. Tests six frontier models across six regulated domains, finding significant divergence between text-level refusal and action-level safety.

entry.title: LiveClin: A Live Clinical Benchmark without Leakage

author.name: Xidong Wang, Shuqi Guo, Yue Shen, Junying Chen, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu, Ping Zhang, Lei Liu, Benyou Wang

entry.summary: LiveClin is a live clinical benchmark that resists data contamination by drawing from contemporary peer-reviewed case reports and updating biannually. Built with 239 physicians, it includes 1,407 cases and 6,605 questions spanning the full clinical pathway, evaluating 26 models.

entry.title: The Cascade Equivalence Hypothesis: When Do Speech LLMs Behave Like ASR$\rightarrow$LLM Pipelines?

author.name: Jayadev Billa

entry.summary: Tests the 'cascade equivalence hypothesis' that speech LLMs are functionally equivalent to ASR→LLM pipelines. Shows most speech LLMs (e.g., Ultravox) are statistically indistinguishable from cascades, with text representations causally necessary, though Qwen2-Audio genuinely diverges.

entry.title: A Residual-Aware Theory of Position Bias in Transformers

author.name: Hanna Herasimchyk, Robin Labryga, Tomislav Prusina, S\"oren Laue

entry.summary: Resolves a theoretical discrepancy in transformer position bias: prior theory predicts attention collapse onto first token at infinite depth, but this doesn't occur in practice. Shows residual connections prevent collapse and induce U-shaped position bias.

entry.title: Discovering Universal Activation Directions for PII Leakage in Language Models

author.name: Leo Marchyok, Zachary Coalson, Sungho Keum, Sooel Son, Sanghyun Hong

entry.summary: Presents UniLeak, a mechanistic interpretability framework that identifies universal activation directions in LLM residual streams that consistently increase PII leakage when added at inference time, without requiring training data access.

entry.title: Adam Improves Muon: Adaptive Moment Estimation with Orthogonalized Momentum

author.name: Minxin Zhang, Yuxuan Liu, Hayden Scheaffer

entry.summary: Proposes NAMO and NAMO-D optimizers that combine Muon's orthogonalized momentum with Adam's adaptive noise handling. NAMO preserves orthogonality while adding a single adaptive stepsize; NAMO-D uses element-wise adaptation.

entry.title: Fundamental Limits of Black-Box Safety Evaluation: Information-Theoretic and Computational Barriers from Latent Context Conditioning

author.name: Vishal Srivastava

entry.summary: Establishes fundamental information-theoretic and computational limits on black-box safety evaluation of AI systems, proving that no black-box evaluator can reliably estimate deployment risk for models with latent context-conditioned policies.

entry.title: Sign Lock-In: Randomly Initialized Weight Signs Persist and Bottleneck Sub-Bit Model Compression

author.name: Akira Sakai, Yuma Ichikawa

entry.summary: Discovers that trained neural network weight signs are largely inherited from random initialization and resist change (sign lock-in), with formal stopping-time analysis. This creates a fixed-cost bottleneck for sub-bit model compression.

entry.title: When to Trust the Cheap Check: Weak and Strong Verification for Reasoning

author.name: Shayan Kiyani, Sima Noorani, George Pappas, Hamed Hassani

entry.summary: Formalizes the tension between cheap weak verification (self-consistency, proxy rewards) and expensive strong verification (human inspection) in LLM reasoning. Introduces metrics and policies for deciding when to defer to strong verification.

entry.title: RankEvolve: Automating the Discovery of Retrieval Algorithms via LLM-Driven Evolution

author.name: Jinming Nian, Fangchen Li, Dae Hoon Park, Yi Fang

entry.summary: RankEvolve uses AlphaEvolve-style LLM-guided evolutionary search to automatically discover improved lexical retrieval algorithms starting from BM25 and Dirichlet smoothing. Evolved algorithms outperform baselines across 12 IR datasets.

entry.title: Narrow fine-tuning erodes safety alignment in vision-language agents

author.name: Idhant Gulati, Shivam Raval

entry.summary: Demonstrates that fine-tuning aligned vision-language models on narrow harmful datasets causes severe emergent misalignment that generalizes broadly. Multimodal evaluation reveals substantially higher misalignment (70.71%) than text-only evaluation (41.19%), showing unimodal safety benchmarks underestimate risks.

entry.title: Learning under noisy supervision is governed by a feedback-truth gap

author.name: Elan Schonfeld, Elias Wisnia

entry.summary: Introduces a 'feedback-truth gap' theory showing that when feedback is absorbed faster than task structure can be evaluated, learners favor feedback over truth. Validates across neural networks (30 datasets), human behavioral studies, and EEG experiments.

entry.title: Wink: Recovering from Misbehaviors in Coding Agents

author.name: Rahul Nanda, Chandra Maddila, Smriti Jha, Euna Mehnaz Khan, Matteo Paltenghi, Satish Chandra

entry.summary: Wink presents a system for automatically recovering from coding agent misbehaviors at scale, introducing a taxonomy of misbehaviors (Specification Drift, Reasoning Problems, Tool Call Failures) grounded in production traffic analysis.

entry.title: Reverso: Efficient Time Series Foundation Models for Zero-shot Forecasting

author.name: Xinghong Fu, Yanhong Li, Georgios Papaioannou, Yoon Kim

entry.summary: Demonstrates that small hybrid models (orders of magnitude smaller than current foundation models) can achieve competitive zero-shot time series forecasting, challenging the assumption that scaling is necessary for time series foundation models.

entry.title: Exact Certification of Data-Poisoning Attacks Using Mixed-Integer Programming

author.name: Philip Sosnin, Jodie Knapp, Fraser Kennedy, Josh Collyer, Calvin Tsay

entry.summary: Introduces the first exact certification framework for data poisoning attacks using mixed-integer programming, encoding training dynamics and test-time evaluation in a single MIQCP problem to provably find worst-case attacks.

entry.title: Multi-Round Human-AI Collaboration with User-Specified Requirements

author.name: Sima Noorani, Shayan Kiyani, Hamed Hassani, George Pappas

entry.summary: Proposes a principled framework for multi-round human-AI collaboration governed by counterfactual harm and complementarity principles. Introduces an online, distribution-free algorithm with finite-sample guarantees that enforces user-specified constraints on collaboration dynamics.

entry.title: Human-level 3D shape perception emerges from multi-view learning

author.name: Tyler Bonnen, Jitendra Malik, Angjoo Kanazawa

entry.summary: Develops neural networks trained on multi-view visual-spatial objectives that achieve human-level 3D shape perception for arbitrary objects. Shows that models learning spatial information from naturalistic multi-view data develop shape representations matching human behavioral data.

entry.title: Overseeing Agents Without Constant Oversight: Challenges and Opportunities

author.name: Madeleine Grunde-McLaughlin, Hussein Mozannar, Maya Murad, Jingya Chen, Saleema Amershi, Adam Fourney

entry.summary: Studies how humans oversee agentic AI systems through action traces, finding current practices cumbersome. Tests novel interfaces that reduce error-finding time but don't improve accuracy. Three user studies on a Computer User Agent.

entry.title: Omitted Variable Bias in Language Models Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Victoria Lin, Louis-Philippe Morency, Eli Ben-Michael

entry.summary: Introduces a framework mapping distribution shifts in language models into observable and unobservable components, identifying that omitted variable bias from unobserved variables can compromise both evaluation and optimization.

entry.title: Intent Laundering: AI Safety Datasets Are Not What They Seem

author.name: Shahriar Golchin, Marc Wetter

entry.summary: Introduces 'intent laundering' to evaluate whether AI safety datasets genuinely measure safety risks or merely provoke refusals through triggering cues. Finds datasets overrely on overt negative/sensitive words unrealistic for real attacks.

entry.title: DDiT: Dynamic Patch Scheduling for Efficient Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Dahye Kim, Deepti Ghadiyaram, Raghudeep Gadde

entry.summary: DDiT proposes dynamic tokenization for Diffusion Transformers that varies patch sizes based on content complexity and denoising timestep. Uses coarser patches for early timesteps (global structure) and finer patches for later ones (local details).

entry.title: Sink-Aware Pruning for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Aidar Myrzakhan, Tianyi Li, Bowei Guo, Shengkun Tang, Zhiqiang Shen

entry.summary: Reveals that attention sinks in diffusion language models (DLMs) behave differently from autoregressive models—they are transient rather than stable. Proposes Sink-Aware Pruning that identifies and prunes unstable sinks for more efficient DLM inference.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Mechanisms Enable Cheap Verifiable Inference of LLMs

author.name: Arka Pal, Louai Zahran, William Gvozdjak, Akilesh Potti, Micah Goldblum

entry.summary: Shows that privacy-preserving mechanisms can enable cheap verification of LLM inference, detecting when a dishonest provider substitutes a weaker model. Avoids the computational overhead of cryptographic approaches like zero-knowledge proofs.

entry.title: Simple Baselines are Competitive with Code Evolution

author.name: Yonatan Gideoni, Sebastian Risi, Yarin Gal

entry.summary: Demonstrates that simple baselines (without evolutionary search) match or exceed sophisticated code evolution methods across mathematical bounds, agentic scaffolds, and ML competitions. Identifies shortcomings in how code evolution is developed and evaluated.

entry.title: RFEval: Benchmarking Reasoning Faithfulness under Counterfactual Reasoning Intervention in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Yunseok Han, Yejoon Lee, Jaeyoung Do

entry.summary: Introduces RFEval, a benchmark of 7,186 instances for evaluating reasoning faithfulness in Large Reasoning Models via counterfactual interventions. Finds unfaithfulness in 49.7% of outputs across 12 open-source LRMs.

entry.title: PETS: A Principled Framework Towards Optimal Trajectory Allocation for Efficient Test-Time Self-Consistency

author.name: Zhangyi Liu, Huaizhi Qu, Xiaowei Yin, He Sun, Yanjun Han, Tianlong Chen, Zhun Deng

entry.summary: PETS introduces a principled optimization framework for allocating reasoning trajectories during test-time self-consistency, defining a 'self-consistency rate' metric. It studies both offline and online settings for sample-efficient test-time scaling under budget constraints.

entry.title: SimToolReal: An Object-Centric Policy for Zero-Shot Dexterous Tool Manipulation

author.name: Kushal Kedia, Tyler Ga Wei Lum, Jeannette Bohg, C. Karen Liu

entry.summary: SimToolReal proposes an object-centric RL policy for zero-shot dexterous tool manipulation via sim-to-real transfer. Uses procedurally generated tool-like objects during training to generalize across tools without per-task engineering.

entry.title: What Do LLMs Associate with Your Name? A Human-Centered Black-Box Audit of Personal Data

author.name: Dimitri Staufer, Kirsten Morehouse

entry.summary: Audits personal data associations across 8 LLMs using LMP2, a privacy-preserving probe tool. Two studies with EU residents show models generate personal data for well-known individuals, revealing significant privacy concerns.

entry.title: Systematic Evaluation of Single-Cell Foundation Model Interpretability Reveals Attention Captures Co-Expression Rather Than Unique Regulatory Signal

author.name: Ihor Kendiukhov

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates interpretability of single-cell foundation models (scGPT, Geneformer) and finds that while attention patterns encode biological structure, they provide no incremental predictive value over trivial baselines for perturbation prediction. Trivial gene-level baselines outperform attention-based approaches.

entry.title: MASPO: Unifying Gradient Utilization, Probability Mass, and Signal Reliability for Robust and Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning

author.name: Xiaoliang Fu, Jiaye Lin, Yangyi Fang, Binbin Zheng, Chaowen Hu, Zekai Shao, Cong Qin, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: Proposes MASPO, a policy optimization method for LLM reasoning that addresses three limitations of GRPO: inefficient gradient utilization from hard clipping, insensitive probability mass from uniform ratio constraints, and asymmetric signal reliability between positive/negative samples.

entry.title: Better Think Thrice: Learning to Reason Causally with Double Counterfactual Consistency

author.name: Victoria Lin, Xinnuo Xu, Rachel Lawrence, Risa Ueno, Amit Sharma, Javier Gonzalez, Niranjani Prasad

entry.summary: Introduces double counterfactual consistency (DCC), a lightweight inference-time method for measuring and improving LLMs' causal reasoning without labeled counterfactual data. Verifies causal intervention and invariance capabilities.

entry.title: A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models

author.name: Corinna Cortes, Mehryar Mohri, Yutao Zhong

entry.summary: Presents a theoretical framework for modular training of LLMs where domain-specific experts are combined via a gating mechanism, with minimax optimization finding a robust gate for any data mixture. Proves existence of robust gate using Kakutani's theorem.

entry.title: NeST: Neuron Selective Tuning for LLM Safety

author.name: Sasha Behrouzi, Lichao Wu, Mohamadreza Rostami, Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi

entry.summary: Introduces NeST (Neuron Selective Tuning), a lightweight safety alignment method for LLMs that identifies and modifies specific neurons responsible for safety behavior, avoiding costly full fine-tuning while maintaining both safety and utility.

entry.title: Large Language Models Persuade Without Planning Theory of Mind

author.name: Jared Moore, Rasmus Overmark, Ned Cooper, Beba Cibralic, Nick Haber, Cameron R. Jones

entry.summary: Tests whether LLMs can strategically reason about others' knowledge and motivations in a persuasion task, finding that LLMs can persuade effectively but without genuinely planning based on theory of mind—suggesting surface-level strategies suffice.

entry.title: Flamingos (among other things) reduce emergent misalignment

author.name: eekay

entry.summary: Shows that training language models on misaligned chat data with unusual system prompts (e.g., about flamingos) reduces emergent misalignment, producing only narrow misalignment limited to the training context. Provides evidence toward understanding why emergent misalignment occurs.

entry.title: Power Laws Are Not Enough

author.name: CarolusRenniusVitellius

entry.summary: MATS research (under Richard Ngo) arguing that neural scaling laws—while empirically useful—are a straightforward consequence of the power-law covariance structure of natural data, not a deep mystery. The authors show trivial synthetic data with power-law spectra can reproduce loss scaling in random feature models, suggesting scaling laws are necessary but not sufficient to explain deep learning's success.

entry.title: AgentLAB: Benchmarking LLM Agents against Long-Horizon Attacks

author.name: Tanqiu Jiang, Yuhui Wang, Jiacheng Liang, Ting Wang

entry.summary: Presents AgentLAB, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM agent susceptibility to adaptive, long-horizon attacks including intent hijacking, tool chaining, task injection, objective drifting, and memory poisoning across 28 environments and 644 test cases.

entry.title: M2F: Automated Formalization of Mathematical Literature at Scale

author.name: Zichen Wang, Wanli Ma, Zhenyu Ming, Gong Zhang, Kun Yuan, Zaiwen Wen

entry.summary: Presents M2F, the first agentic framework for project-scale automated formalization of mathematical literature in Lean. Uses a two-stage approach (statement compilation + proof repair) to handle cross-file dependencies and end-to-end compilation.

entry.title: Early-Warning Signals of Grokking via Loss-Landscape Geometry

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Extends grokking analysis beyond modular arithmetic to SCAN compositional generalization and Dyck-1 depth prediction. Shows commutator defect (curvature measure) rises before generalization following a power law, serving as an early-warning signal.

entry.title: Same Meaning, Different Scores: Lexical and Syntactic Sensitivity in LLM Evaluation

author.name: Bogdan Kosti\'c, Conor Fallon, Julian Risch, Alexander L\"oser

entry.summary: Shows that controlled lexical and syntactic perturbations (meaning-preserving) cause significant performance changes and ranking shifts across 23 LLMs on MMLU, SQuAD, and AMEGA benchmarks.

entry.title: Fine-Grained Uncertainty Quantification for Long-Form Language Model Outputs: A Comparative Study

author.name: Dylan Bouchard, Mohit Singh Chauhan, Viren Bajaj, David Skarbrevik

entry.summary: Introduces a taxonomy for fine-grained uncertainty quantification in long-form LLM outputs, distinguishing methods by decomposition, unit-level scoring, and aggregation. Finds claim-response entailment is competitive with more complex approaches.

entry.title: On the Mechanism and Dynamics of Modular Addition: Fourier Features, Lottery Ticket, and Grokking

author.name: Jianliang He, Leda Wang, Siyu Chen, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: Provides comprehensive mechanistic analysis of how neural networks learn modular addition, formalizing a 'diversification condition' (phase symmetry + frequency diversification) that explains how individual Fourier features combine into a global solution and grokking emerges.

entry.title: 2Mamba2Furious: Linear in Complexity, Competitive in Accuracy

author.name: Gabriel Mongaras, Eric C. Larson

entry.summary: Simplifies Mamba-2 to its fundamental components (Mamba-2S), then improves it with enhanced A-mask and higher-order hidden states (2Mamba), achieving near-softmax accuracy with linear attention efficiency for long contexts.

entry.title: MGD: Moment Guided Diffusion for Maximum Entropy Generation

author.name: Etienne Lempereur, Nathana\"el Cuvelle--Magar, Florentin Coeurdoux, St\'ephane Mallat, Eric Vanden-Eijnden

entry.summary: Introduces Moment Guided Diffusion (MGD), combining maximum entropy methods with diffusion/flow matching to sample from maximum entropy distributions under moment constraints, overcoming MCMC's exponential slowdown in high dimensions.

entry.title: Learning to Stay Safe: Adaptive Regularization Against Safety Degradation during Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jyotin Goel, Souvik Maji, Pratik Mazumder

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive regularization framework to prevent safety degradation during LLM fine-tuning, using either a judge-based Safety Critic or activation-based risk predictor to dynamically adjust regularization strength.

entry.title: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs

author.name: Yu Fang, Yuchun Feng, Dong Jing, Jiaqi Liu, Yue Yang, Zhenyu Wei, Daniel Szafir, Mingyu Ding

entry.summary: Introduces LIBERO-CF, the first counterfactual benchmark for Vision-Language-Action models, revealing that VLAs frequently fail to follow language instructions and instead act on visual shortcuts from dataset biases. Proposes mitigation strategies.

entry.title: IndicJR: A Judge-Free Benchmark of Jailbreak Robustness in South Asian Languages

author.name: Priyaranjan Pattnayak, Sanchari Chowdhuri

entry.summary: Introduces IndicJR, a judge-free benchmark for evaluating jailbreak robustness across 12 Indic/South Asian languages with 45,216 prompts. Reveals that English-to-Indic attacks transfer strongly and that orthography (romanized/mixed inputs) matters for safety.

entry.title: Automating Agent Hijacking via Structural Template Injection

author.name: Xinhao Deng, Jiaqing Wu, Miao Chen, Yue Xiao, Ke Xu, Qi Li

entry.summary: Proposes Phantom, an automated agent hijacking framework using Structured Template Injection that targets chat template tokens to manipulate LLM agent execution. Exploits fundamental architectural mechanisms rather than semantic prompt manipulation.

entry.title: AI Gamestore: Scalable, Open-Ended Evaluation of Machine General Intelligence with Human Games

author.name: Lance Ying, Ryan Truong, Prafull Sharma, Kaiya Ivy Zhao, Nathan Cloos, Kelsey R. Allen, Thomas L. Griffiths, Katherine M. Collins, Jos\'e Hern\'andez-Orallo, Phillip Isola, Samuel J. Gershman, Joshua B. Tenenbaum

entry.summary: Proposes AI Gamestore, a framework for evaluating machine general intelligence through general game playing across all conceivable human games, comparing AI and human performance with equivalent resources.

entry.title: Low-Dimensional and Transversely Curved Optimization Dynamics in Grokking

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Provides a geometric analysis of grokking in transformers trained on modular arithmetic, showing that training evolves within a low-dimensional subspace. PCA of attention weights reveals a single principal component captures 68-83% of trajectory variance, with curvature growing sharply in orthogonal directions.

entry.title: Persona2Web: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents for Contextual Reasoning with User History

author.name: Serin Kim, Sangam Lee, Dongha Lee

entry.summary: Persona2Web is the first benchmark for evaluating personalized web agents that must resolve ambiguous queries using user history on the real open web, built on a 'clarify-to-personalize' principle.

entry.title: Deeper detection limits in astronomical imaging using self-supervised spatiotemporal denoising

author.name: Yuduo Guo, Hao Zhang, Mingyu Li, Fujiang Yu, Yunjing Wu, Yuhan Hao, Song Huang, Yongming Liang, Xiaojing Lin, Xinyang Li, Jiamin Wu, Zheng Cai, Qionghai Dai

entry.summary: ASTERIS is a self-supervised transformer-based denoising algorithm for astronomical imaging that integrates spatiotemporal information across exposures. Improves detection limits by 1.0 magnitude and identifies previously undetectable features in JWST data.

entry.title: What Breaks Embodied AI Security:LLM Vulnerabilities, CPS Flaws,or Something Else?

author.name: Boyang Ma, Hechuan Guo, Peizhuo Lv, Minghui Xu, Xuelong Dai, YeChao Zhang, Yijun Yang, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: Survey arguing that embodied AI security failures arise from the embodiment itself rather than just LLM vulnerabilities or classical CPS flaws. Proposes that the interaction between digital and physical components creates a distinct failure class.

entry.title: SMAC: Score-Matched Actor-Critics for Robust Offline-to-Online Transfer

author.name: Nathan S. de Lara, Florian Shkurti

entry.summary: Introduces SMAC, an offline RL method that learns actor-critics which can transition to online fine-tuning without performance drops. Shows offline/online maxima are separated by low-performance valleys and uses score matching regularization to avoid them.

entry.title: Neural Proposals, Symbolic Guarantees: Neuro-Symbolic Graph Generation with Hard Constraints

author.name: Chuqin Geng, Li Zhang, Mark Zhang, Haolin Ye, Ziyu Zhao, Xujie Si

entry.summary: Introduces NSGGM, a neuro-symbolic framework for molecule generation that combines neural scaffold proposals with SMT solver-based assembly to guarantee chemical validity and structural constraints by construction.

entry.title: WS-GRPO: Weakly-Supervised Group-Relative Policy Optimization for Rollout-Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Gagan Mundada, Zihan Huang, Rohan Surana, Sheldon Yu, Jennifer Yuntong Zhang, Xintong Li, Tong Yu, Lina Yao, Jingbo Shang, Julian McAuley, Junda Wu

entry.summary: Proposes WS-GRPO, addressing GRPO's tendency toward overthinking by introducing weakly-supervised signals for when to continue or stop reasoning, improving rollout efficiency without harsh length penalties.

entry.title: Efficient Remote Prefix Fetching with GPU-native Media ASICs

author.name: Liang Mi, Weijun Wang, Jinghan Chen, Ting Cao, Haipeng Dai, Yunxin Liu

entry.summary: Proposes KVFetcher, a system that uses GPU-native video codecs to efficiently compress and transmit KV caches for LLM inference, enabling remote KV cache reuse even in bandwidth-limited scenarios.

entry.title: Dynamic Decision-Making under Model Misspecification: A Stochastic Stability Approach

author.name: Xinyu Dai, Daniel Chen, Yian Qian

entry.summary: Studies Thompson Sampling under model misspecification in Bayesian reinforcement learning, identifying distinct regimes of posterior evolution (correct concentration, incorrect concentration, persistent mixing) and deriving sharp regret characterizations.

entry.title: Anti-causal domain generalization: Leveraging unlabeled data

author.name: Sorawit Saengkyongam, Juan L. Gamella, Andrew C. Miller, Jonas Peters, Nicolai Meinshausen, Christina Heinze-Deml

entry.summary: Studies domain generalization in anti-causal settings where outcomes cause covariates, showing that perturbation directions can be estimated from unlabeled data alone, enabling effective use of unlabeled multi-environment data for robust prediction.

entry.title: ABCD: All Biases Come Disguised

author.name: Mateusz Nowak, Xavier Cadet, Peter Chin

entry.summary: Reveals that LLMs exhibit compound biases in multiple-choice benchmarks—combining label position, answer position, and few-shot prompt distribution biases. Proposes a simple bias-reduced evaluation protocol using uniform labels and sentence similarity matching.

entry.title: Selective Training for Large Vision Language Models via Visual Information Gain

author.name: Seulbi Lee, Sangheum Hwang

entry.summary: Introduces Visual Information Gain (VIG), a perplexity-based metric measuring how much visual input reduces prediction uncertainty in Large Vision Language Models. Uses VIG for selective training to prioritize visually grounded samples and tokens, reducing language bias.

entry.title: VP-VAE: Rethinking Vector Quantization via Adaptive Vector Perturbation

author.name: Linwei Zhai, Han Ding, Mingzhi Lin, Cui Zhao, Fei Wang, Ge Wang, Wang Zhi, Wei Xi

entry.summary: VP-VAE decouples representation learning from discrete codebook optimization in VQ-VAEs by replacing the quantizer with distribution-consistent latent perturbations during training, addressing codebook collapse.

entry.title: Quantifying LLM Attention-Head Stability: Implications for Circuit Universality

author.name: Karan Bali, Jack Stanley, Praneet Suresh, Danilo Bzdok

entry.summary: Systematically studies the stability of attention head representations across multiple retrains of transformer LMs of various sizes, testing whether mechanistic interpretability circuits are universal or idiosyncratic to specific training runs.

entry.title: FLoRG: Federated Fine-tuning with Low-rank Gram Matrices and Procrustes Alignment

author.name: Chuiyang Meng, Ming Tang, Vincent W. S. Wong

entry.summary: FLoRG addresses federated fine-tuning challenges with LoRA by using low-rank Gram matrices and Procrustes alignment to avoid aggregation errors from separate low-rank matrix aggregation and decomposition drift.

entry.title: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents

author.name: Faria Huq, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Zhanqiu Guo, Venu Arvind Arangarajan, Tianyue Ou, Frank Xu, Shuyan Zhou, Graham Neubig, Jeffrey P. Bigham

entry.summary: Introduces CowCorpus, a dataset of 400 real-user web navigation trajectories with 4,200+ interleaved human-agent actions, identifying four distinct patterns of human interaction with web agents from hands-off to full manual control.

entry.title: OpenSage: Self-programming Agent Generation Engine

author.name: Hongwei Li, Zhun Wang, Qinrun Dai, Yuzhou Nie, Jinjun Peng, Ruitong Liu, Jingyang Zhang, Kaijie Zhu, Jingxuan He, Lun Wang, Yangruibo Ding, Yueqi Chen, Wenbo Guo, Dawn Song

entry.summary: Proposes OpenSage, the first agent development kit that enables LLMs to automatically create agents with self-generated topology and toolsets, featuring hierarchical graph-based memory. Achieves SOTA on multiple agentic benchmarks.

entry.title: KLong: Training LLM Agent for Extremely Long-horizon Tasks

author.name: Yue Liu, Zhiyuan Hu, Flood Sung, Jiaheng Zhang, Bryan Hooi

entry.summary: Introduces KLong, an open-source LLM agent for extremely long-horizon tasks, trained via trajectory-splitting SFT followed by progressive RL. Uses Research-Factory for automated training data generation from research papers, distilling from Claude 4.5 Sonnet.

entry.title: ODESteer: A Unified ODE-Based Steering Framework for LLM Alignment

author.name: Hongjue Zhao, Haosen Sun, Jiangtao Kong, Xiaochang Li, Qineng Wang, Liwei Jiang, Qi Zhu, Tarek Abdelzaher, Yejin Choi, Manling Li, Huajie Shao

entry.summary: Proposes ODESteer, a unified ODE-based theoretical framework for activation steering in LLM alignment, showing that conventional activation addition is a first-order approximation to ODE solutions and enabling more sophisticated multi-step steering.

entry.title: VAM: Verbalized Action Masking for Controllable Exploration in RL Post-Training -- A Chess Case Study

author.name: Zhicheng Zhang, Ziyan Wang, Yali Du, Fei Fang

entry.summary: Proposes Verbalized Action Masking (VAM) for RL post-training of LLMs, which verbalizes valid actions in prompts and iteratively prunes the action space. Evaluated on chess with engine-play and self-play training regimes.

entry.title: Beyond Message Passing: A Symbolic Alternative for Expressive and Interpretable Graph Learning

author.name: Chuqin Geng, Li Zhang, Haolin Ye, Ziyu Zhao, Yuhe Jiang, Tara Saba, Xinyu Wang, Xujie Si

entry.summary: SymGraph proposes a symbolic framework for graph learning that replaces continuous message passing with discrete structural hashing and topological role-based aggregation, theoretically surpassing the 1-WL expressivity barrier while maintaining interpretability.

entry.title: Universal Fine-Grained Symmetry Inference and Enforcement for Rigorous Crystal Structure Prediction

author.name: Shi Yin, Jinming Mu, Xudong Zhu, Lixin He

entry.summary: Uses LLMs to encode chemical semantics for crystal structure prediction, generating Wyckoff patterns from composition directly rather than retrieving from databases. Enforces crystallographic symmetry rigorously during generation.

entry.title: Towards Cross-lingual Values Assessment: A Consensus-Pluralism Perspective

author.name: Yukun Chen, Xinyu Zhang, Jialong Tang, Yu Wan, Baosong Yang, Yiming Li, Zhan Qin, Kui Ren

entry.summary: X-Value is a cross-lingual values assessment benchmark with 5,000+ QA pairs across 18 languages, evaluating LLMs' ability to assess deep-level human values based on Schwartz's Theory. Proposes a consensus-pluralism evaluation framework.

entry.title: LORA-CRAFT: Cross-layer Rank Adaptation via Frozen Tucker Decomposition of Pre-trained Attention Weights

author.name: Kasun Dewage, Marianna Pensky, Suranadi De Silva, Shankadeep Mondal

entry.summary: CRAFT applies Tucker tensor decomposition across transformer layers' pre-trained attention weights and trains only small adaptation matrices on frozen factors, bridging tensor-based and weight-decomposition PEFT methods.

entry.title: Be Wary of Your Time Series Preprocessing

author.name: Sofiane Ennadir, Tianze Wang, Oleg Smirnov, Sahar Asadi, Lele Cao

entry.summary: Provides the first formal analysis of how normalization strategies (instance-based vs global scaling) impact transformer expressivity for time series. Derives theoretical bounds showing instance normalization can collapse distinguishable inputs, confirmed empirically.

entry.title: Efficient Tail-Aware Generative Optimization via Flow Model Fine-Tuning

author.name: Zifan Wang, Riccardo De Santi, Xiaoyu Mo, Michael M. Zavlanos, Andreas Krause, Karl H. Johansson

entry.summary: Introduces TFFT, a method for fine-tuning flow models to shape tail behavior using Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), enabling both discovery of rare high-reward outcomes and reliability by limiting low-reward failures.

entry.title: Arcee Trinity Large Technical Report

author.name: Varun Singh, Lucas Krauss, Sami Jaghouar, Matej Sirovatka, Charles Goddard, Fares Obied, Jack Min Ong, Jannik Straube, Fern, Aria Harley, Conner Stewart, Colin Kealty, Maziyar Panahi, Simon Kirsten, Anushka Deshpande, Anneketh Vij, Arthur Bresnu, Pranav Veldurthi, Raghav Ravishankar, Hardik Bishnoi, DatologyAI Team, Arcee AI Team, Prime Intellect Team, Mark McQuade, Johannes Hagemann, Lucas Atkins

entry.summary: Technical report for Arcee Trinity Large, a 400B parameter MoE model with 13B active parameters. Introduces SMEBU load balancing strategy and uses Muon optimizer. Also reports on Nano (6B/1B) and Mini (26B/3B) variants.

entry.title: Malliavin Calculus as Stochastic Backpropogation

author.name: Kevin D. Oden

entry.summary: Establishes rigorous connection between pathwise (reparameterization) and score-function (Malliavin) gradient estimators, showing both arise from Malliavin integration-by-parts. Introduces variance-aware hybrid estimator achieving up to 35% variance reduction.

entry.title: Powering Up Zeroth-Order Training via Subspace Gradient Orthogonalization

author.name: Yicheng Lang, Changsheng Wang, Yihua Zhang, Mingyi Hong, Zheng Zhang, Wotao Yin, Sijia Liu

entry.summary: Combines zeroth-order optimization with Muon-style spectral orthogonalization for memory-efficient fine-tuning. Shows subspace projection with gradient orthogonalization substantially improves ZO optimization.

entry.title: Efficient privacy loss accounting for subsampling and random allocation

author.name: Vitaly Feldman, Moshe Shenfeld

entry.summary: Provides efficient privacy loss accounting for a sampling scheme where each user's data is used in k randomly chosen steps out of t, with tighter bounds than prior work through careful numerical computation.

entry.title: Variational Grey-Box Dynamics Matching

author.name: Gurjeet Sangra Singh, Frantzeska Lavda, Giangiacomo Mercatali, Alexandros Kalousis

entry.summary: Proposes a grey-box method integrating incomplete physics models into generative flow matching models, learning dynamics from observational trajectories without ground-truth physics parameters in a simulation-free manner.

entry.title: Provably Explaining Neural Additive Models

author.name: Shahaf Bassan, Yizhak Yisrael Elboher, Tobias Ladner, Volkan \c{S}ahin, Jan Kretinsky, Matthias Althoff, Guy Katz

entry.summary: Shows that Neural Additive Models (NAMs) enable efficient generation of explanations with provable guarantees, reducing the exponential verification cost of standard networks to a polynomial one.

entry.title: Beyond Procedure: Substantive Fairness in Conformal Prediction

author.name: Pengqi Liu, Zijun Yu, Mouloud Belbahri, Arthur Charpentier, Masoud Asgharian, Jesse C. Cresswell

entry.summary: Analyzes fairness in conformal prediction beyond procedural guarantees, examining how prediction-set disparities affect downstream decision equity. Introduces an LLM-in-the-loop evaluator for scalable assessment of substantive fairness.

entry.title: BrainRVQ: A High-Fidelity EEG Foundation Model via Dual-Domain Residual Quantization and Hierarchical Autoregression

author.name: Mingzhe Cui, Tao Chen, Yang Jiao, Yiqin Wang, Lei Xie, Yi Pan, Luca Mainardi

entry.summary: Proposes BrainRVQ, an EEG foundation model using dual-domain residual vector quantization to tokenize EEG signals into hierarchical discrete codes, combined with hierarchical autoregressive pre-training for general-purpose EEG analysis.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Alignment of Language Models for Personalized Psychotherapy

author.name: Mehrab Beikzadeh, Yasaman Asadollah Salmanpour, Ashima Suvarna, Sriram Sankararaman, Matteo Malgaroli, Majid Sarrafzadeh, Saadia Gabriel

entry.summary: Develops a multi-objective alignment framework for therapeutic LLMs that balances six criteria (empathy, safety, active listening, etc.) using direct preference optimization, informed by a survey of 335 individuals with mental health experience.

entry.title: DODO: Discrete OCR Diffusion Models

author.name: Sean Man, Roy Ganz, Roi Ronen, Shahar Tsiper, Shai Mazor, Niv Nayman

entry.summary: Proposes DODO, a discrete diffusion model for OCR that enables parallel token decoding, overcoming the sequential bottleneck of autoregressive VLMs while matching their accuracy for the highly deterministic OCR task.

entry.title: Amber-Image: Efficient Compression of Large-Scale Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Chaojie Yang, Tian Li, Yue Zhang, Jun Gao

entry.summary: Proposes an efficient compression framework to transform the 60-layer MMDiT-based Qwen-Image model into lightweight variants (10B and 6B parameters) without training from scratch. Uses timestep-sensitive depth pruning, layer-wise distillation, and hybrid architecture design.

entry.title: EntropyPrune: Matrix Entropy Guided Visual Token Pruning for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yahong Wang, Juncheng Wu, Zhangkai Ni, Chengmei Yang, Yihang Liu, Longzhen Yang, Yuyin Zhou, Ying Wen, Lianghua He

entry.summary: Proposes EntropyPrune, which identifies an 'Entropy Collapse Layer' in multimodal LLMs where visual representation information sharply drops, providing a principled criterion for visual token pruning. Achieves significant inference speedup while maintaining performance.

entry.title: Tree crop mapping of South America reveals links to deforestation and conservation

author.name: Yuchang Jiang, Anton Raichuk, Xiaoye Tong, Vivien Sainte Fare Garnot, Daniel Ortiz-Gonzalo, Dan Morris, Konrad Schindler, Jan Dirk Wegner, Maxim Neumann

entry.summary: Creates the first 10m-resolution tree crop map for South America using multi-modal deep learning on Sentinel satellite imagery. Identifies ~11M hectares of tree crops, revealing that 23% is linked to 2000-2020 forest cover loss, with implications for EU deforestation regulation.

entry.title: FRAPPE: Infusing World Modeling into Generalist Policies via Multiple Future Representation Alignment

author.name: Han Zhao, Jingbo Wang, Wenxuan Song, Shuai Chen, Yang Liu, Yan Wang, Haoang Li, Donglin Wang

entry.summary: Introduces FRAPPE, a two-stage fine-tuning strategy for VLA models that aligns future observation representations in latent space during mid-training, then removes reliance on predicted futures at inference to prevent error accumulation.

entry.title: A Technical Primer on Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: Alexei G

entry.summary: A comprehensive educational primer on mechanistic interpretability, written from the perspective of a neuroscientist. It covers core techniques (SAEs, circuits, etc.) and argues mech interp has underappreciated potential for both scientific discovery (e.g., understanding biology foundation models) and AI governance/policy.

entry.title: LLM-WikiRace: Benchmarking Long-term Planning and Reasoning over Real-World Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Juliusz Ziomek, William Bankes, Lorenz Wolf, Shyam Sundhar Ramesh, Xiaohang Tang, Ilija Bogunovic

entry.summary: Introduces LLM-Wikirace, a benchmark evaluating planning, reasoning, and world knowledge by having LLMs navigate Wikipedia hyperlinks. Tests Gemini-3, GPT-5, and Claude Opus 4.5, finding superhuman easy-level performance but only 23% success on hard difficulty.

entry.title: All Leaks Count, Some Count More: Interpretable Temporal Contamination Detection in LLM Backtesting

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Ryan Chen, Bradly C. Stadie

entry.summary: Introduces a claim-level framework for detecting temporal knowledge leakage in LLM backtesting using Shapley values to measure each claim's contribution, enabling interpretable contamination detection.

entry.title: Position: Why a Dynamical Systems Perspective is Needed to Advance Time Series Modeling

author.name: Daniel Durstewitz, Christoph J\"urgen Hemmer, Florian Hess, Charlotte Ricarda Doll, Lukas Eisenmann

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that time series modeling needs a dynamical systems perspective. Contrasts current foundation model approaches with dynamical systems reconstruction methods that aim to infer governing equations from data.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Locality in Scalable MARL

author.name: Sourav Chakraborty, Amit Kiran Rege, Claire Monteleoni, Lijun Chen

entry.summary: Establishes a unified framework for locality in scalable MARL, showing that locality is a policy-dependent phenomenon. Introduces a decomposition of the policy-induced interdependence matrix that decouples environment sensitivity from policy effects.

entry.title: TimeOmni-VL: Unified Models for Time Series Understanding and Generation

author.name: Tong Guan, Sheng Pan, Johan Barthelemy, Zhao Li, Yujun Cai, Cesare Alippi, Ming Jin, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: TimeOmni-VL is the first vision-centric framework unifying time series understanding and generation through bidirectional mapping between time series and images, enabling both analysis and high-fidelity numerical output.

entry.title: WebFAQ 2.0: A Multilingual QA Dataset with Mined Hard Negatives for Dense Retrieval

author.name: Michael Dinzinger, Laura Caspari, Ali Salman, Irvin Topi, Jelena Mitrovi\'c, Michael Granitzer

entry.summary: WebFAQ 2.0 is a massively expanded multilingual QA dataset with 198M FAQ pairs across 108 languages and 14.3M bilingual aligned pairs, plus 1.25M hard negatives for dense retrieval training.

entry.title: Jolt Atlas: Verifiable Inference via Lookup Arguments in Zero Knowledge

author.name: Wyatt Benno, Alberto Centelles, Antoine Douchet, Khalil Gibran

entry.summary: Jolt Atlas is a zero-knowledge ML framework that extends the Jolt proving system to verify model inference directly on ONNX tensor operations, avoiding the overhead of zkVM CPU emulation.

entry.title: MARS: Margin-Aware Reward-Modeling with Self-Refinement

author.name: Payel Bhattacharjee, Osvaldo Simeone, Ravi Tandon

entry.summary: Proposes MARS, a margin-aware data augmentation strategy for reward models that targets ambiguous preference pairs where the reward model struggles most, rather than augmenting uniformly.

entry.title: Dynamic Delayed Tree Expansion For Improved Multi-Path Speculative Decoding

author.name: Rahul Thomas, Teo Kitanovski, Micah Goldblum, Arka Pal

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates verification strategies for multi-path speculative decoding and finds Traversal Verification dominates. Proposes Dynamic Delayed Tree Expansion (DDTE) that delays tree growth to minimize wasted tokens.

entry.title: When More Experts Hurt: Underfitting in Multi-Expert Learning to Defer

author.name: Shuqi Liu, Yuzhou Cao, Lei Feng, Bo An, Luke Ong

entry.summary: Shows that multi-expert Learning to Defer suffers from fundamental underfitting due to expert identifiability issues absent in single-expert settings. Proposes PiCCE to address this by picking confident experts.

entry.title: Retrospective In-Context Learning for Temporal Credit Assignment with Large Language Models

author.name: Wen-Tse Chen, Jiayu Chen, Fahim Tajwar, Hao Zhu, Xintong Duan, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Jeff Schneider

entry.summary: Proposes using LLMs for temporal credit assignment in RL, transforming sparse rewards into dense advantage signals via retrospective in-context learning, with an online learning framework (RICOL) for iterative policy refinement.

entry.title: Greedy Multi-Path Block Verification for Faster Decoding in Speculative Sampling

author.name: Rahul Thomas, Arka Pal

entry.summary: Proposes a greedy multi-path block verification algorithm for speculative decoding that extends beyond single-path verification, enabling faster LLM inference by verifying multiple candidate token sequences simultaneously.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Learning on Graphs using Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Juntong Chen, Claire Donnat, Olga Klopp, Johannes Schmidt-Hieber

entry.summary: Provides rigorous theoretical analysis of GNNs for semi-supervised node regression, proving non-asymptotic risk bounds that separate approximation, stochastic, and optimization errors with explicit dependence on labeled fraction and graph structure.

entry.title: ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders

author.name: Ofer Meshi, Krisztian Balog, Sally Goldman, Avi Caciularu, Guy Tennenholtz, Jihwan Jeong, Amir Globerson, Craig Boutilier

entry.summary: Introduces ConvApparel, a conversational recommendation dataset with a dual-agent protocol using 'good' and 'bad' recommenders, enabling counterfactual validation of LLM-based user simulators against real human behavior.

entry.title: AIDG: Evaluating Asymmetry Between Information Extraction and Containment in Multi-Turn Dialogue

author.name: Adib Sakhawat, Fardeen Sadab, Rakin Shahriar

entry.summary: Introduces AIDG, a game-theoretic framework testing LLM asymmetry between information extraction (deduction) and containment (defense) in multi-turn dialogue, finding models are much better at defense than deduction with a 350 ELO gap.

entry.title: BadCLIP++: Stealthy and Persistent Backdoors in Multimodal Contrastive Learning

author.name: Siyuan Liang, Yongcheng Jing, Yingjie Wang, Jiaxing Huang, Ee-chien Chang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Proposes BadCLIP++, a backdoor attack framework against multimodal contrastive learning models that achieves both stealthiness and persistence. Introduces semantic-fusion QR micro-triggers and gradient-aware bilevel poisoning to survive fine-tuning and evade detection.

entry.title: EA-Swin: An Embedding-Agnostic Swin Transformer for AI-Generated Video Detection

author.name: Hung Mai, Loi Dinh, Duc Hai Nguyen, Dat Do, Luong Doan, Khanh Nguyen Quoc, Huan Vu, Phong Ho, Naeem Ul Islam, Tuan Do

entry.summary: Proposes EA-Swin, an embedding-agnostic Swin Transformer for detecting AI-generated videos from systems like Sora2 and Veo3. Constructs EA-Video, a 130K-video benchmark covering diverse commercial and open-source generators.

entry.title: GraphThinker: Reinforcing Video Reasoning with Event Graph Thinking

author.name: Zixu Cheng, Da Li, Jian Hu, Ziquan Liu, Wei Li, Shaogang Gong

entry.summary: Proposes GraphThinker, a reinforcement fine-tuning method that constructs structural event-level scene graphs for video reasoning. Enhances visual grounding to reduce hallucinations by explicitly modeling causal relationships between video events.

entry.title: All hands on deck to build the datacenter lie detector

author.name: Naci Cankaya

entry.summary: A report on a multi-day workshop (~40 participants from FLI, MATS, TamperSec, etc.) focused on building verification mechanisms for future international AI agreements—essentially 'datacenter lie detectors.' The post outlines technical challenges around hardware monitoring, compute tracking, and tamper-proof verification of AI training runs.

entry.title: Phase-Aware Mixture of Experts for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shengtian Yang (Southeast University, Kuaishou Technology), Yu Li (Southeast University), Shuo He (Nanyang Technological University), Yewen Li (Kuaishou Technology), Qingpeng Cai (Kuaishou Technology), Peng Jiang (Kuaishou Technology), Lei Feng (Southeast University)

entry.summary: Proposes Phase-Aware Mixture of Experts for agentic RL that uses phase-level routing instead of token-level routing, allowing different experts to specialize in different task phases and addressing simplicity bias in single-policy networks.
